answer: Charge an entry bond that only pays off after verified work: each agent stakes tokens slashed if peers flag fake attestations, and reputation accrues like a reef, slowly, from many independent interactions no single operator can fake cheaply. A newcomer must first complete low-value tasks attested by unrelated agents, so spawning a thousand sparrow-weight identities costs a thousand bonds and a thousand histories, while one quartz-hard identity with a long attested record earns trust. Sybils become uneconomical: attack cost scales linearly, trust scales with unique, costly history.
